question.text: A horizontal line $l$ passes through the point $(5,4).$ Calculate the coordinates of the $y$-intercept of $l.$
question.explanation:
On any horizontal line, all points have the same $y$-coordinate.

The $y$-coordinate of the point $(5,4)$ is $4,$ so the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept is also $4.$

Therefore, the coordinates of the $y$-intercept are $(0,4).$

question.text: A horizontal line $l$ passes through the point $(-3,2).$ What are the coordinates of the $y$-intercept of $l?$
question.explanation:
On any horizontal line, all points have the same $y$-coordinate.

The $y$-coordinate of the point $(-3,2)$ is $2,$ so the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept is also $2.$

Therefore, the coordinates of the $y$-intercept are $\left(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2}\right).$

question.text: The equation of the line that passes through the points $(2,8)$ and $(4,4)$ is $\,y=$
question.explanation:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points: \begin{align*} m &= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\\[5pt] &=\frac{4 -8}{4 - 2}\\[5pt] &=\frac{-4}{2}\\[5pt] &=-2 \end{align*}

Substituting the slope $m=-2$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach \[ y = -2x + b. \]

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(4,4)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} y &= -2x + b\\[5pt] 4 &= -2(4) +b\\[5pt] 4 &=-8+b\\[5pt] 4+8 &=b\\[5pt] 12 &=b \end{align*}

So the equation of the line is $y=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-2}\,x + \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{12}.$
